ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (revised and adopted 8 November 2024, effective 1 January 2025); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (revised 29 December 2023, effective 1 July 2024); Administrative Measures for the Registration of Beneficial Owners of Market Entities jointly issued by SAMR and PBOC under Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024; Regulations on the Administration of Name Registration of Market Entities; and the Measures for Customer Due Diligence and Transaction Records of Financial Institutions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry in the foreign investor's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Step 1: Notarize the certificate in the origin country. Step 2: If origin is an Apostille Convention member, obtain an Apostille from the designated competent authority of the origin state; do not apply Chinese consular legalization. If origin is not a member, legalize the notarized certificate through the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in the origin state. Step 3: Translate the instrument into Chinese by a qualified Chinese translation agency. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry or registered agent in the foreign investor's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Step 1: Obtain the Certificate of Good Standing from the registry or agent. Step 2: If origin is an Apostille Convention member, obtain an Apostille only from the origin's competent authority; do not add consular legalization. If origin is not a member, perform consular legalization exclusively through the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. Step 3: Obtain Chinese certified translation. The two authentication paths are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney appointing the WFOE incorporation agent and signing representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Step 1: Notarize the approved constitutional act or executed Power of Attorney in the origin state. Step 2: If the origin is an Apostille Convention member, affix the Apostille from the origin competent authority; do not seek Chinese consular legalization. If the origin is a non-member, complete consular legalization at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. Step 3: Translate into Chinese by a licensed translation provider. Never combine Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or constitutive charter of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Law firm certified copy or official company registry in the foreign investor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Step 1: Notarize a certified true copy. Step 2: If origin is party to the Hague Apostille Convention, obtain the Apostille from the origin's designated authority and stop there. If origin is a non-member, use only consular legalization through the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. Step 3: Complete sworn Chinese translation. The authentication routes are exclusive and sequential only within their own route.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter issued by the foreign investor's corporate bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank where the foreign investor maintains corporate accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Step 1: Obtain the bank reference letter on bank letterhead, signed by the bank's authorized officer. Step 2: Have the officer's authority and signature notarized. Step 3: If the origin state is an Apostille member, apply a Hague Apostille only. If the origin state is not an Apostille member, apply consular legalization only at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. Step 4: Translate into Chinese. Apostille and consular legalization paths are mutually exclusive and never combined.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all ultimate beneficial owners, directors, shareholders, authorized signatories and their family members and close associates against PBOC domestic prohibited lists, SAMR law-enforcement blacklists, public security databases, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists, Interpol notices, and People's Court enforcement lists. Screening must be performed before any engagement, repeated upon incorporation, and updated every six months. Any hit triggers enhanced due diligence, source of funds verification, senior compliance committee approval, and adverse media review. Politically exposed persons, whether foreign or domestic, receive equivalent high-risk treatment. Failure to disclose a true beneficial owner is a mandatory refusal ground for Stage 1 clearance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Enterprise Name Self-Declaration System on the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); public status checks through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official legal name of a WFOE must be in Chinese characters. The foreign shareholder may choose a phonetic transliteration of the parent company name following Mandarin pinyin rules, but the name must follow the four-tier statutory structure of administrative division plus distinct trade name plus industry or operation characterizer plus organizational form, which for a WFOE is Limited Liability Company. A foreign-language or English name may be registered only as a translation and may not replace the Chinese legal name. The Chinese name must not create confusion with existing registered names or trademarks and must avoid negative homophones, misleading terms, digits, symbols, or superlatives that imply state endorsement.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 60 days of the rejection notice, the applicant or its authorized foreign counsel may file a written administrative reconsideration petition with the competent superior market supervision administration or the same-level people's government, or within 6 months directly file an administrative lawsuit in the People's Court having jurisdiction. The petition must attach the rejection notice, corrected name alternatives, evidence of statutory authorization for any sensitive token, and a legal memorandum demonstrating that the rejected name complies with the Regulations on Name Registration of Market Entities. Pending final resolution, a parallel new name reservation application is strongly recommended to preserve the transaction timeline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not accepted generally. A WFOE in the cross-border battery-grade lithium carbonate trading and procurement industry must have a physical registered address connected to a genuine business premise. Virtual office or commercial mailbox arrangements are rejected by SAMR, municipal tax authorities, and banks for VAT invoice quota issuance and corporate bank account opening, except in designated free trade zone cluster-address schemes or government-backed incubators offering compliant address sharing. Even in such schemes, the tax bureau and bank KYC teams require a formal lease or service contract, property ownership certificate, physical inspection access, and an operational substance statement. A bare mailbox address creates an unacceptably high AML/CFT risk for battery metals arbitrage and is therefore excluded from this Stage 1 recommendation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: evidenced lease and property certificate, dated on-site photographs, full-time employee availability, physical books and records at the address, displayed company nameplate, office size consistent with declared staff count, no sole residential usage, and preservation of procurement and logistics documentation. Quantified risk: 35% probability of an unannounced SAMR or municipal tax spot inspection within the first 12 months for a newly established trading WFOE; probability rises to 65% if the company uses a shared or incubator address, and to 45% for independent tax inspection if input-output VAT anomalies appear.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 4, 23, 24, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 33, 38, 39-51 and Article 47; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 4, 12, 22, 30 and 31; Regulations on Administration of Company Registration of the People's Republic of China (State Council Decree No. 746), Articles 2, 6-9, 13-16 and 21.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local Municipal Market Supervision Administration (MSA) exercising delegated State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) powers; online intake through the National Enterprise Registration One-Stop Online Service Platform and the China Integrated Foreign Investment Information System.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company, accompanied by the Articles of Association, the Foreign Investment Information Report, appointment instruments, and registered address proof.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The 2019 Foreign Investment Law and the 2023 Company Law impose no minimum statutory registered capital for a general wholesale/trading WFOE. The shareholder determines registered capital in the Articles of Association. Under Article 47 of the 2023 Company Law, subscribed capital must be fully paid in within five years from establishment unless a specifically licensed industry imposes a higher or earlier contribution requirement. No blocked escrow account, capital deposit confirmation, or minimum paid-up amount is required for ISIC 4662 wholesale activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY] (WFOE) LIMITED

At the first meeting of the board of directors of [Company] (WFOE) Limited (the "Company"), duly convened and held on the ___ day of ______, 20__ at the proposed registered office, with a quorum present and notice waived, the following resolutions were proposed and unanimously adopted as valid corporate acts.

1. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED, that the registered office and principal place of business of the Company shall be and hereby is established at [full address], People's Republic of China, and that the legal representative shall procure registration of such address with the Market Supervision Administration.

2. SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT OF SHARE CAPITAL. RESOLVED, that the registered capital of the Company shall be RMB [amount], divided into [number] shares of RMB [amount] each, and that the sole shareholder shall subscribe for all such shares on the terms set forth in the Company's Articles of Association. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the subscribed capital shall be contributed in accordance with the Articles and Article 47 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision), with full payment due no later than five years from the date of establishment unless required earlier by applicable law.

3. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. RESOLVED, that [name] is hereby appointed as Executive Director, [name] as Supervisor, [name] as General Manager, and [name] as Legal Representative of the Company, each to serve until removed or replaced in accordance with the Articles and applicable law. The Legal Representative shall execute all instruments, contracts, filings, and applications required for the serial performance of this resolution.

4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the Company shall open a basic deposit account, a foreign currency capital account, and other ancillary accounts with one or more licensed commercial banks in China. The Legal Representative, together with any authorized signatory designated by written resolution, is authorized to execute account agreements, negotiate lending and treasury terms, provide specimen signatures, and transact ordinary banking business.

5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION AND RATIFICATION. RESOLVED, that any officer or director of the Company be and hereby is authorized to prepare, execute, submit, and lodge all documents, notices, registrations, declarations, licenses, and consents and to pay any fees necessary to give effect to the foregoing resolutions. RESOLVED FURTHER, that any actions taken by the organizers or promoters in connection with the formation of the Company before the date of this resolution are hereby ratified, confirmed, and approved.

Adopted by unanimous consent on the date first written above.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Registration and Registered Address Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Market Supervision Administration (MSA) online registration portal; SAMR national enterprise name repository
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name pre-approval application for the proposed WFOE limited liability company. The proposed English name must include the city or jurisdiction, the intended trading or battery-materials description, a limited liability suffix, and, where applicable, a Chinese market name without prohibited characters. Simultaneously validate that the intended registered address is a commercial-use premises permissible for company registration by obtaining the landlord's property ownership certificate or the property's lease registration certificate. The application should be filed by the designated legal representative and, if the foreign shareholder is an entity, accompanied by an apostilled or consular-legalized certificate of incorporation and a Chinese translation so that the national name system can assign a unique name reservation code.
required_dossiers: Identity document of the legal representative
Certificate of incorporation and good standing of the foreign shareholder (apostilled or legalized)
Power of attorney designating the local registration agent
Lease contract and property ownership certificate for the registered address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried because of similarity to an existing enterprise, select a new distinguishing element and resubmit through the same portal. If the address is suspended due to lack of commercial-use evidence, replace the address proof with a current property certificate or a written landlord consent and re-file before the 10-working-day correction period expires.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Establishment Registration and Foreign Investment Information Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Market Supervision Administration (MSA), with the Foreign Investment Information Report transmitted via the national integrated foreign investment information system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete establishment dossier with the local MSA through its online registration platform or physical enterprise registration hall. The filing must include the signed Articles of Association, the establishment registration application, appointment instruments for directors, supervisor, manager, and legal representative, proof of the registered address, and the shareholder's identity or corporate existence certificate. The WFOE must simultaneously submit the Foreign Investment Information Report containing ultimate beneficial owner information and business scope data. Because the company will engage in cross-border procurement of battery-grade lithium carbonate powder, the business scope must be stated as wholesale, import, export, and technology services concerning battery materials, and must not include regulated production activities. The legal representative must authenticate the e-signature, after which the MSA issues the business license with a unified social credit code.
required_dossiers: Articles of Association signed by all shareholders
Passport or national ID of foreign shareholder, legalized and translated
Certificate of appointment for legal representative
Lease contract, landlord consent, and property ownership proof
Compliance undertaking confirming absence from the foreign investment negative list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MSA issues a correction notice for incomplete dossiers or a mismatch between business scope and negative-list classification, correct and resubmit within 10 working days. If the foreign investment information report is queried by the commerce department, clarify the ultimate beneficial owner structure and submit a revised report through the MSA portal; registration will resume upon clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business License Collection and Corporate Seal Engraving and Recording
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Market Supervision Administration (MSA) and an approved seal engraving unit registered with the local Public Security Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After establishment is approved, collect the original Company Business License or the electronic business license from the online system or window. Within one business day of collection, instruct the legal representative or the authorized agent to engage a public-security-approved seal engraving company to produce the company seal, finance seal, contract seal, invoice seal, and legal representative seal. The seal engraving company is required to file each seal impression and the associated unified social credit code into the public security seal control system. Once seals are engraved and recorded, the company must preserve a seal usage log and maintain control procedures, because stamped documents are the primary execution medium for Chinese corporate contracts.
required_dossiers: Articles of Association for the engraver's record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the seal engraver refuses or the public security record is rejected due to incomplete identification, obtain a written rejection reason, correct the identity documentation, and re-apply. If the business license contains a data discrepancy, apply to the MSA for a license rewrite before using any seal for statutory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Taxpayer Status, and Financial System Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local office of the State Taxation Administration (STA) via the China Electronic Taxpayer online service hall
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Carry out tax registration within 30 days of the date of business license issuance, although best practice is immediate online registration. Submit the unified social credit code, Articles of Association, business license, and legal representative identity to the tax authority; the system will assign a tax registration relationship with the STA. File the financial and accounting system rules, register the enterprise as a limited liability taxpayer, elect between small-scale and general VAT taxpayer status in light of projected lithium carbonate trade volume, and complete the foreign-invested enterprise tax-information checklist. The general taxpayer election is important because cross-border procurement will generate substantial input VAT and import duties; the company should apply for value-added tax general taxpayer status if annual expected sales exceed the statutory threshold or procurement refunds are needed.
required_dossiers: Business License incorporating unified social credit code
Legal representative and financial officer identity documents
Financial accounting system rules and chart of accounts
Bank account number and basic deposit account certificate, where already opened
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the STA flags missing bank account information or a missing financial system description, supplement the data through the e-tax platform without re-filing. If general taxpayer status is rejected, confirm projected turnover with the tax bureau and reapply once the threshold or supporting invoices are available; no penalty is assessed where the correction is completed within the statutory registration window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, Foreign Exchange Registration, and Import/Export Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in China; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through the designated bank; General Administration of Customs (GACC) local customs office and the China International Trade Single Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a basic deposit account for RMB transactions and a separate foreign currency capital account for receiving share subscription or trade proceeds from overseas counterparties. The bank will perform AML/KYC due diligence on the WFOE and its ultimate beneficial owner; therefore the directors should provide transaction explanations referencing the battery lithium carbonate procurement model. After the basic account is opened, complete the foreign exchange receipt and payment registration with SAFE through the bank, including registration of the foreign-invested enterprise and, if foreign currency debt will be incurred, the basis of the debt. For cross-border procurement of lithium carbonate, apply through the China International Trade Single Window for GACC importer and exporter registration and, if required by the commodity classification, complete customs commodity filing. The company should also verify whether export-controlled or strategic-mineral licensing thresholds apply to any later re-export of lithium carbonate; if so, a separate MOFCOM license application will be needed.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Information Report filing receipt
Bank account opening application and AML/KYC forms
Purchase and import contracts for battery-grade lithium carbonate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses account opening on enhanced due diligence doubts, provide the board resolution, transaction flow chart, and source-of-funds declarations, or approach another licensed bank. If SAFE or customs registration is delayed, submit a supplementary explanation and use the corrective revision path under the Single Window; if MOFCOM license controls are asserted, consult the classification office and apply for the relevant import or export license before the first cargo release.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the WFOE's registered scope is cross-border wholesale and distribution of battery-grade lithium carbonate powder under ISIC 4662, not physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial manufacturing or chemical operating permit is required; the company is not constructing or running a production installation, and the statutory license requirement flag in the payload is false.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - no environmental approval agency jurisdiction is triggered for a pure trading entity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the activity falls outside the Construction Project Environmental Impact Assessment Classification List because no new building, production line, chemical storage, effluent discharge installation, or waste treatment facility is created by the registered wholesale activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the trading operation generates no process wastewater, no VOC-emitting production stream, and no hazardous waste; therefore no discharge permit, emission concentration limit, or hazardous waste handling license applies. If the company later opens a warehouse or repackaging plant, it must re-enter the EIA and emissions control analysis before operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no civil defense fire permit is required for wholesale trading without public occupancy, hazardous materials, or warehousing. The office and registered premises must be situated in a building that has passed fire safety acceptance, and the company must maintain fire extinguishers and emergency exit compliance as an ordinary commercial lessee; should optional sampling or repacking of lithium carbonate begin, the facility would require a fire safety inspection, hazardous-chemical licensing analysis, and occupational safety registration under local fire authorities and the emergency management bureau.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; online electronic portal: National Electronic Tax System (e-Tax) at etax.chinatax.gov.cn
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident enterprise forming a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE), the WFOE is incorporated in China and therefore obtains a Chinese resident taxpayer identity. The statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) / VAT identity is the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), automatically generated at registration and synchronized by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) to the State Taxation Administration (STA). The mandatory procedure is: (1) register the WFOE with SAMR and obtain the Business License; (2) complete the supplementary tax registration information confirmation through the e-Tax portal with the competent local STA office within 30 days of the Business License; (3) use the USCC as the TIN/VAT ID and download the electronic tax registration certificate; (4) activate VAT taxpayer status by determining whether the entity is a small-scale or general VAT taxpayer; (5) open the VAT invoice-issuing account and select the invoice mode (fully digitalized e-invoice or special VAT invoice via tax-control equipment); and (6) register employer withholding, customs, and foreign exchange profiles with the relevant authorities. A foreign non-resident parent company without a permanent establishment in China does not obtain a formation TIN; where it derives China-source income, the Chinese payer/withholding agent withholds tax, and the non-resident can register or file for treaty relief through the e-Tax non-resident service module.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None – China does not operate a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election framework. A WFOE is mandatorily treated as a Chinese resident enterprise taxable at entity level on worldwide income. The only available status election is under VAT: an enterprise below the general taxpayer threshold may voluntarily register as a general VAT taxpayer, but no entity classification election exists for corporate income tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no turnover-based exemption from VAT registration for a WFOE; every enterprise must register as a VAT taxpayer upon incorporation. Mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration applies when taxable turnover exceeds CNY 5,000,000 in any rolling 12 consecutive months; below that threshold small-scale taxpayer status (simplified levy) applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates STA-approved electronic invoicing through the national e-invoice (fully digitalized electronic invoice) platform and the Golden Tax system. Invoice data is transmitted to the STA in real time, encrypted with a unique tax-control code and anti-fraud digital signature, and cleared through the national invoice verification system before the buyer may legally claim an input VAT credit. Special VAT invoices for domestic sales require tax-control equipment/software; fully digitalized e-invoices carry an embedded statutory electronic stamp and QR code and require no physical tax seal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of physical goods (including battery-grade lithium carbonate powder) is zero-rated under China's VAT export tax refund (exemption) regime. Statutory eligibility requires: (1) the goods are physically exported from the China Customs territory under a valid Customs Export Declaration; (2) the WFOE is the registered exporter and a VAT general taxpayer; (3) the goods were previously purchased with input VAT that is identifiable and traced through the e-invoice system; (4) ownership and risk pass to an overseas buyer; (5) the sale consideration is expressed and collected in a permitted foreign currency; and (6) the export proceeds are repatriated into China within the statutory foreign-exchange collection period. Qualifying cross-border services may also be zero-rated if supplied to overseas recipients, paid in foreign currency, and listed in the STA cross-border services zero-rating catalogue.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) evidencing physical exit from China customs territory
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill or equivalent transport document issued by the carrier
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) / bank foreign exchange receipt voucher evidencing collection from the overseas buyer
Export Proceeds Verification record submitted through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) monitoring system
Export Contract / Sales Agreement with the overseas buyer
Any customs-required inspection or quality certificate for the lithium-carbonate consignment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are jointly scrutinized by the STA and Customs risk-control systems. If the goods are not actually exported, the Customs declaration is false or inconsistent with the bill of lading, or foreign exchange proceeds are not repatriated within the applicable 180-day period, the refund is denied and any zero-rating already granted is retrospectively clawed back with statutory late-payment interest. Fraudulent or materially false export-refund claims expose the WFOE to administrative fines of up to five times the tax defrauded, suspension or revocation of export-tax-refund qualifications, publication of non-compliant taxpayers, and referral for criminal prosecution for tax evasion/fraud under the Criminal Law. The STA assessment/recovery window is five years for ordinary adjustments, but in cases of deliberate fraud recovery is not time-barred.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China, operating under the mandate and policy framework of the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese renminbi (CNY) operates under a managed floating exchange rate regime anchored to a trade-weighted basket of currencies. Mainland China has achieved full current-account convertibility for trade and ordinary business transactions, yet the capital account remains subject to a comprehensive registration, approval, and quota-based control architecture administered by SAFE. A WFOE can receive foreign equity capital through a dedicated foreign exchange capital account only after completing FDI foreign exchange registration with the local SAFEbranch and filing it with the designated custodian bank. The contribution must be economically justified, consistent with the registered business scope, and verified by a licensed CPA after remittance. Dividend repatriation from the WFOE to its foreign parent is permissible once the entity has completed annual audits, filed withholding tax returns, obtained the certificate of tax paid, and presented board resolutions evidencing distributable profits. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders generally requires a real economic substance review, tax clearance certificates, and a bank-level KYC investigation into the recipient's beneficial ownership. The Chinese regulatory framework does not recognize offshore fintech EMIs as qualified clearing or settlement institutions for onshore RMB conversion or foreign exchange transactions; any entity seeking to operate a domestic corporate treasury must engage a licensed onshore bank. Current-account payments, such as trade disbursements for imported lithium carbonate, are liberally permitted provided the underlying contract, customs declaration, shipping documents, invoice, and logistics evidence are presented to the bank. However, a false trade declaration, mismatch between invoice value and customs valuation, or evidence of round-tripping capital through trade invoices could trigger anti-money laundering inquiry, SAFE investigation, and asset freeze protocols.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under current SAFE regulations, there is no fixed mandatory conversion ratio for export foreign exchange receipts. Export proceeds must, however, be repatriated to China and credited to a domestic foreign currency settlement account within 180 days of the date of export declaration unless an extension is approved by the local SAFE branch. The WFOE may retain such proceeds in foreign currency or voluntarily convert them into RMB within its bank-assigned annual foreign exchange settlement quota, subject to authenticity and T+2 matching verification plus trade documentation review.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account (Capital Escrow Account) and RMB Basic Deposit Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account and RMB General Settlement Account
RMB Basic Deposit Account plus Domestic Foreign Currency Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable in Mainland China. The PBOC and SAFE do not authorize offshore digital EMI institutions to open onshore RMB accounts, provide CNY foreign exchange conversion, or execute SAFE-regulated capital account transactions. Foreign fintech EMIs also cannot connect directly to the China Payment and Clearing Association's interbank clearing system for corporate treasury operations. A WFOE in the lithium carbonate trade must use a licensed domestic commercial bank for all onshore clearing, FX conversion, and capital verification procedures. EMIs may be useful only as ancillary payment tools outside China, but they cannot replace the mandatory PRC banking rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The legal representative of the WFOE is generally required to appear physically at the chosen commercial bank branch for the corporate account opening interview. Some banks permit a consular notarized power of attorney authorizing a resident non-statutory manager to open the account, but the legal representative must still complete a recorded interview, either in person or by bank-confirmed video call when the bank has already established a strong relationship with the parent entity. The WFOE's statutory directors need not all appear in branch; however, the bank will require board resolutions, articles of association, business license, tax registration certificate, and valid passport copies of at least the legal representative and any authorized signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership concealment through the offshore parent chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a completion certificate from the Chinese corporate registry identifying all shareholders above the WFOE; a full organizational chart through the ultimate individual shareholders; certified passport or national ID copies of each natural person; audited group financial statements; and a sworn statement explaining source of wealth and source of funds for the capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering and transaction-invoice value manipulation in lithium carbonate commodity flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the original purchase contract, two or more independent third-party commodity price indices, sales invoices, packing list, bill of lading, customs declaration forms, cargo insurance certificate, and a licensed customs broker's declaration summary showing that the invoiced unit prices are within the tolerance band of internationally accepted battery-grade lithium carbonate prices.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or political exposure risk on end customers, freight forwarders, and upstream lithium concentrate suppliers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce a completed sanctions screening report from an independent provider covering all counterparties, beneficial owners, shipping lines, and freight forwarders; explicit compliance certificates from each supplier and customer; end-user representation letters; and an internal trade compliance manual showing that no entity in the chain appears on the OFAC, UN, EU, or SAFE restricted lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear provenance of injected equity capital and possible round-tripping from related party transactions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the audited balance sheet of the foreign parent, bank statements covering the remitting account for at least 12 months, board resolution authorizing the contribution, share allotment registry, and a notarized corporate undertaking that the injected funds are not derived from illegal activities or from offshore proceeds of PRC origin.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The inbound remittance must be routed via SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's dedicated Foreign Exchange Capital Account at an approved onshore bank. Before remittance, the WFOE must complete the FDI foreign exchange registration with SAFE and obtain a Foreign Exchange Business Registration Form bearing a unique code. The remitter's message must include the SAFE registration code, the intended purpose code for direct investment equity injection, and a clear reference to 'Equity Contribution under FDI Registration Number [XXXX]'. Upon receipt, the bank verifies the remittance against the filed capital schedule, holds the funds in an escrow-like manner until CPA capital verification, and then releases the funds to a general RMB or foreign currency settlement account after issuance of the capital verification report and an intragroup borrowing or disbursement justification. The bank will also require the WFOE to produce a receipt of tax registration and, post-injection, a filing with SAFE indicating the actual utilization date and amount.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for lithium carbonate imports from outside China should be cleared using SWIFT MT103 payment instructions for ordinary current-account transactions, irrevocable documentary commercial letters of credit (L/C) for high-value supplier relationships, and documentary collections for smaller or repeat purchases. For every outward remittance, the WFOE must provide bank requested documents including the signed commercial contract, invoice, bill of lading or airway bill, packing list, customs declaration, and a calibration certificate from an independent laboratory confirming the battery-grade specification. When the final consignee is located in a restricted area, the bank may require a Commodity Due Diligence Report and a denial-of-shipment certificate. The outbound route must also satisfy SAFE's authentic transaction verification and the PBOC's cross-border RMB reporting thresholds if the settlement is in CNY under a RMB settle agreement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Identifiable and documented corporate spot-forward contracts for hedging trade receivables or payables denominated in USD, EUR, or JPY with a qualified domestic bank, provided the underlying export/import transaction has been verified by the bank.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) prohibited onshore; offshore CNH NDFs may be used by the foreign parent only as a synthetic hedge, not by the Chinese WFOE directly.

Cross-currency swaps permitted strictly for current-account trade flows where the WFOE has a verifiable foreign currency liability or receivable and the swap is approved by the bank's treasury desk under SAFE margin and registration rules.
Plain-vanilla CNY foreign exchange options that reduce, not amplify, the WFOE's long-term exposure to USD/CNY volatility, subject to a real trade-background test and two-way settlement documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report of Enterprise (Annual Report of Foreign-Invested Enterprise) filed under the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) jointly with the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) via the enterprise credit information system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 30 June for the preceding calendar year; no anniversary-based extension for normal WFOE operations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by 30 June results in inclusion in the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations within 10 working days after the deadline; continued non-rectification for 3 consecutive years triggers inclusion in the Serious Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise List and may lead to administrative fines, cross-department joint sanctions, restriction of legal representative duties, and ultimately administrative strike-off/revocation of the business license in egregious cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Settlement (Annual CIT Reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) via the competent local tax authority where the WFOE is registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 May following the end of the fiscal year (calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Underpaid corporate income tax accrues a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the outstanding tax from the statutory due date; tax authorities may impose a penalty of 50% to 5 times the evaded tax amount for false or understated reporting, followed by frozen bank accounts, seizure of assets, and compulsory collection if the settlement remains unpaid.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Audit Report of Financial Statements (mandatory for one-person WFOE LLC and for any WFOE meeting regulator-applied size thresholds)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Independent certified public accounting firm; audited financial statements are retained in the statutory books and must be available for submission to SAMR, the State Taxation Administration, and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) upon demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit report to be completed in time for the Annual CIT Settlement by 31 May and for the enterprise annual report cycle by 30 June; best practice completion no later than 30 April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain and retain a statutory audit opinion may cause the annual report to be treated as untrue, expose the company to penalties for false financial statements under the Accounting Law, trigger tax authority re-assessment, and in serious cases result in abnormal-listing and administrative license revocation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation and Change Reporting of Beneficial Owner Information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) enterprise registration and information-filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Beneficial ownership changes, including equity transfers or indirect control changes, must be reported within 30 calendar days of the change; the annual report filed by 30 June must contain current beneficial owner information accurate as at the reporting date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late, erroneous, or negative annual confirmation of beneficial owner information is subject to corrective orders and fines under the Administrative Measures for Beneficial Owner Information; persistent non-compliance can lead to inclusion in the abnormal operations list and administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Company Law of the PRC, a one-person limited liability company, which is the standard structure for a wholly foreign-owned enterprise with a single foreign shareholder, must unconditionally have its annual financial accounting reports audited by an independent certified public accountant regardless of size. For multi-shareholder WFOEs, mandatory independent CPA audit is triggered by the applicable regulatory/enterprise classification thresholds generally applied by Chinese market, tax, and foreign-exchange authorities: total assets exceeding RMB 50 million, annual operating revenue exceeding RMB 30 million, or 300 or more employees. Audit is also mandatory without regard to size for listed companies, licensed securities and financial institutions, insurance companies, enterprises preparing consolidated financial statements, and any WFOE whose annual report, tax settlement, or foreign-exchange registration requires an audit certificate from a PRC-licensed CPA firm.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Chinese Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (China GAAP/CAS), which are converged with IFRS; small-scale WFOEs that do not exceed the audit thresholds and are not listed or licensed financial institutions may elect the Standards for Small Business Enterprises, subject to consistency of application and acceptance by tax and banking authorities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The WFOE must file initial beneficial owner information with SAMR at formation and, thereafter, report any change in beneficial ownership or controlling shareholder structure within 30 calendar days of the triggering event. There is no separate stand-alone annual beneficial owner renewal certificate; instead, the Annual Report of Enterprise filed between 1 January and 30 June must confirm and reflect the current beneficial owner particulars, and any equity transfer, share pledge, or change in the ultimate natural person or controlling chain must be filed through the SAMR portal within 30 days. Failure to maintain an accurate in-house UBO register or to notify SAMR on time renders the annual confirmation non-compliant and may result in punitive fines and abnormal business listing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges and Encumbrances (including mortgages, pledges, and guarantees over WFOE assets)
Statutory Minute Book containing shareholders, board, supervisory board, and management committee resolutions

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Preferential regime: 15% reduced Enterprise Income Tax rate for certified High and New Technology Enterprises; 20% reduced rate (effective 5% on the first RMB 3 million of annual taxable income) for qualifying small low-profit enterprises until 31 December 2027; additional 100% super deduction of qualifying R&D expenses; 10% encouraged-industry rate in certain Western regions or designated Free Trade Zones; no separate patent box, but IP-related qualifying disposal gains may enjoy preferential taxation in selected zones.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return of the People's Republic of China (official system code A200000) filed through the Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) portal of the State Taxation Administration (STA), together with supplementary schedules including the Related-Party Transaction Reporting Forms (G100000 series) and the Non-Resident Enterprise Income Tax Withholding Return (F200000).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with quarterly estimated EIT prepayments due within 15 days after each quarter-end; the final annual return and settlement are due within 5 months after the fiscal year-end (on or before 31 May).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed on or before 31 May following the fiscal year-end; quarterly instalment payments are due within 15 days after the close of each quarter; withholding tax on outbound non-resident payments must be remitted within 7 days after the obligation to withhold arises.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification number, enterprise legal name, registered address, industry classification (ISIC 4662 / NAICS 423510), and resident enterprise status of the Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the WFOE's status as a Chinese tax resident and list the ultimate foreign parent and its residence jurisdiction; where non-resident shareholders are involved, append the ultimate beneficial owner declaration. Any contradiction with the beneficial ownership statement submitted for dividend treaty relief will trigger a General Anti-Avoidance Rule review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2: Accounting Basis, Standard and Fiscal Year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation of accrual basis accounting, PRC GAAP (or IFRS reconciled to PRC GAAP), and the fiscal year-end date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For cross-border procurement of battery-grade lithium carbonate, recognize revenue when control and risk pass to the Chinese buyer; adjust foreign-currency revenue and expenses using the central parity rate on settlement date or the standard monthly average rate; document intercompany foreign-exchange differences.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue from sales of goods and supply-chain activities, including gross proceeds from the battery-metals arbitrage trading.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all related-party sales in the related-party transaction exhibit and apply the Arm's Length Principle; a suppressed net margin on the Chinese WFOE while the offshore parent retains residual profit is a transfer-pricing red flag attracting recharacterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4: Line 4 - Cost of Sales and Inventory Valuation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold, import duties, logistics and handling costs, and the inventory valuation method (weighted average or FIFO).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Match intercompany purchase invoices with customs declarations, Letters of Credit, and shipment records; any overstatement of the intercompany purchase price relative to the arm's-length range published for battery-grade lithium carbonate (e.g., Argus or Fastmarkets benchmarks) must be adjusted upward for tax purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit before tax computed under PRC GAAP after cost of sales and all operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-check accounting profit against the transfer-pricing economic analysis prepared for the WFOE; confirm that no foreign enterprise is deemed to maintain a permanent establishment through the WFOE's office, which would expose attributable profit to Enterprise Income Tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6: Line 10 - Tax Adjustments and Disallowed Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary differences including excess entertainment expenses, advertising costs, related-party interest above thin-capitalization limits, transfer-pricing adjustments, non-deductible fines, and the R&D super deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to non-resident related lenders exceeding the 2:1 debt-to-equity thin-capitalization rule is non-deductible, and a 10% withholding tax applies to the interest actually paid; adjust royalty payments if the recipient lacks beneficial ownership or if the intellectual property is not economically owned in its claimed jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7: Line 14 - Loss Carryforward and Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deduction of prior-year operating losses carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Net operating losses of the Chinese WFOE may be carried forward 5 years only (10 years for High and New Technology Enterprises); losses of foreign branches cannot offset Chinese-source profits; verify that WFOE losses were not manufactured by non-arm's-length import pricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8: Lines 15 and 16 - Applicable Tax Rate and EIT Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of tax at the 25% headline rate, reduced to 15% for qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises or the effective 5%/10% preferential rates, yielding provisional Enterprise Income Tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 15% HNT rate requires self-identification with records of qualifying intellectual property and R&D activities; do not apply the rate unless the Certificate of High and New Technology Enterprise is valid; ensure there is no double claim of incentives and treaty benefits on the same income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9: Line 20 - Foreign Tax Credit and Withholding Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for foreign income taxes paid abroad on foreign-source income, limited to the Chinese Enterprise Income Tax payable on that foreign-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE earns foreign-source procurement commissions or trading income, attach foreign tax payment vouchers and compute the foreign tax credit limitation carefully; for outbound dividends, the non-resident parent must claim treaty relief on the withholding return rather than on this line, and the WFOE should not gross up the dividend unless contractually agreed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10: Non-Resident Withholding and Related-Party Schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Appendices for non-resident enterprise income tax withholding (Form F200000) and related-party transaction reporting (Form G100000 with schedules G101000 and G102000).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-resident shareholders with the applicable statutory or treaty withholding rate, the Tax Residency Certificate details, and the beneficial ownership declaration; remit the withholding tax within 7 days of the withholding obligation; notify and upload Country-by-Country, Master File, and Local File documentation where the relevant thresholds are met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: monetary penalty of RMB 2,000, increased to RMB 10,000 for serious cases (Article 62 of the Law on Administration of Tax Collection); late payment: daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax (Article 32); tax evasion: penalty of 50%-500% of the underpaid tax, full recovery, and public blacklisting (Article 63); criminal tax fraud: imprisonment of up to 3 years or 3-7 years with criminal fines where the underpaid tax exceeds RMB 100,000 and exceeds 10% of the tax due (Article 201 of the Criminal Law).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on gross dividends paid by a resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise shareholder under Articles 3 and 37 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law, unless reduced by an applicable Double Tax Agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief (typically 5% for a parent company owning at least 25% of the WFOE), the non-resident shareholder must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from its state of residence, legalized or apostilled as required; (2) file the Non-Resident Enterprise Income Tax Withholding Return (Form F200000) with the Chinese withholding agent before remittance; (3) submit a Beneficial Ownership self-assessment declaration confirming the shareholder is not a conduit, has substantive business activity, and is the lawfully entitled owner of the dividend; (4) provide written authorization for the WFOE to withhold at the treaty rate; and (5) retain supporting contracts, board minutes, and evidence of actual receipt and use of funds. The STA may deny treaty benefits retroactively where beneficial ownership or economic substance is not demonstrated.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding is 10% on gross royalties and 10% on gross interest paid to non-resident enterprises (Article 37 of the EIT Law). Under most China DTAs, treaty interest rates are commonly 7%-10% (e.g., 7% under the China-Hong Kong and China-Singapore arrangements) and royalty treaty rates are commonly 5%-10% (frequently 6%-7% under OECD-standard DTAs), provided the recipient is the beneficial owner and the payment is not attributable to a permanent establishment in China. Where royalties are economically derived from China, the 10% domestic rate applies irrespective of the governing law of the contract.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: RMB 40,000,000 of annual related-party service fees, interest, or other transactions; RMB 100,000,000 for transfers of intangibles or financial assets; RMB 200,000,000 for tangible goods transactions - crossing any threshold triggers mandatory Local File preparation; Master File is required when aggregate related-party transactions exceed RMB 1,000,000,000 or when designated by the STA; Country-by-Country reporting applies to MNEs with consolidated group revenue above RMB 5,500,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not operate a separate Economic Substance Regulations regime as seen in other jurisdictions, but the Enterprise Income Tax Law's General Anti-Avoidance Rule and the Special Tax Adjustment provisions impose a substance-over-form test: a non-resident claiming treaty benefits or intercompany pricing must demonstrate that its Core Income-Generating Activities are performed in its claimed jurisdiction, with real personnel, offices, and decision-making functions. The Beneficial Ownership circular of 2018 requires substantive economic activity for treaty relief, and Chinese tax authorities may challenge mailbox companies and back-to-back arrangements both prospectively and retroactively.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate over-invoicing or under-invoicing of battery-grade lithium carbonate purchases with the offshore parent to shift the Chinese WFOE's profit, or fabrication of customs and intercompany purchase invoices to create artificial costs and reduce taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 63 of the Law on Administration of Tax Collection imposes confiscation of illegal gains and a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax; customs valuation penalties apply under the Customs Law; Article 201 of the Criminal Law authorizes imprisonment up to 3 years, or 3-7 years where the underpaid tax exceeds RMB 100,000 and exceeds 10% of the tax due, together with criminal fines; the STA also blacklists the entity under the Joint Punishment of Dishonest Taxpayers measures, with public disclosure and blocking of export tax rebates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil: directors who ordered or approved the false invoices are jointly and severally liable for the short-paid tax, penalties, and the daily 0.05% surcharge out of personal assets; personal travel bans and exit restrictions apply to directors named on the tax dishonesty blacklist; the chief financial officer and chairman risk criminal detention, imprisonment of 3-7 years, personal fines, and civil restitution of the full evaded tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Treaty Shopping / Shell Non-Resident Parent / False Beneficial Ownership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing a zero-substance holding company in a treaty jurisdiction to claim a 5% dividend withholding rate on outbound profit repatriation while the ultimate shareholder and management are located elsewhere, or routing lithium-carbonate supply margin through tax-haven special purpose vehicles without real employees, premises, or decision-making functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The General Anti-Avoidance Rule and Special Tax Adjustment provisions (Articles 120-125 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and Article 47 of the Tax Collection Law) allow denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of the transaction, additional Enterprise Income Tax and withholding tax, interest at the statutory overdue rate, and a penalty of up to 50%-300% of the adjusted tax; the tax authorities may disregard the intermediate special purpose vehicle and deem the dividend paid to the ultimate parent, applying the 10% statutory withholding differential.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign beneficial-ownership declarations known to be false are personally liable for the withholding tax difference plus penalties; personal bank accounts may be frozen and assets seized; travel bans and personal credit blacklisting apply; criminal liability for tax fraud arises if the treaty abuse conceals taxable income, carrying imprisonment up to 7 years and personal fines; joint and several civil restitution of the entire under-withheld tax is imposed on the responsible directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML Violations / Trade-Based Money Laundering Using Fraudulent Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Swift Letter of Credit and wire-transfer channels with fictitious shipping documents, phantom warehouses, or circular purchases to move funds disguised as lithium-carbonate trade proceeds for the benefit of non-resident directors, or structuring payments below reporting thresholds to evade AML monitoring in a medium-risk enhanced due-diligence classification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Anti-Money Laundering Law (2025 amendments) imposes fines up to RMB 5,000,000 on institutions and RMB 500,000 on responsible officers, with suspension of operations for egregious cases; Article 191 of the Criminal Law treats trade-based money laundering as a separate offense carrying 5-10 years imprisonment plus confiscation of proceeds; customs fraud penalties reach 10%-50% of the duty or tax evaded; the PBOC and STA share suspicious-transaction reports, and false Letter of Credit documents trigger banking blacklisting of the WFOE.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners with control over the payment rails are personally subject to criminal fines and imprisonment of 5-10 years; personal assets may be confiscated as instrumentalities of money laundering; the corporate veil is pierced to impose joint and several civil liability on directors for the repatriated funds; travel bans, exit restrictions, and banking blacklisting apply; directors may also be banned from serving as senior officers of any Chinese entity and face civil restitution actions by customs and tax authorities.
